A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present the Horton table, which is a revamped BCHT with remap entries that reduces the average cost of positive and negatives lookups to less than 1.1 buckets while achieving load factors of more than 95%.

we are the first to show that the expected lookup costs of positive and negative queries can be reduced to fewer than 2 and 1.5 buckets, respectively, for a load factor of 95% and that these costs are achieved with a single, primary, and many alternate hash functions.
we present Horton tables, a revamped BCHTs that reduce the expected cost of negative lookups to 1.06 and positive lookups to 0.88 buckets, while still achieving a load factor of 95%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of hash tables is not only a function of the number of elements that can be inserted, but also of the number of cache lines accessed to find them.
the cost of lookups in BCHTs can be greatly reduced by tracking and remapping overflow elements.
the cost of lookups can be reduced significantly while preserving the high load factors and throughput that are critical to data-intensive computing.
